subject: Chemistry
questionText: An unknown primary amide X (C₅H₉NO) is subjected to the Hofmann Bromamide Degradation reaction using Br₂ and aqueous KOH. The resulting primary amine Y is isolated and subjected to the Hinsberg test, forming a sulfonamide derivative that is completely SOLUBLE in aqueous NaOH. When amine Y is treated with HNO₂ at 0–5°C, it liberates N₂ gas ↑ and yields an optically active 2° alcohol Z. What is the structural formula of original amide X?

options.explanation: Yields 1-aminobutane, which on HNO₂ treatment gives butan-1-ol (achiral).

1. Amide X (C₅H₉NO) undergoes Hofmann degradation to yield 1° amine Y with one carbon less (C₄H₁₁N). 2. 1° amine Y with HNO₂ yields an optically active 2° alcohol Z (C₄H₁₀O). 3. The only optically active 2° four-carbon alcohol is Butan-2-ol (CH₃-C*H(OH)-CH₂CH₃). 4. Amine Y yielding Butan-2-ol must be sec-butylamine (CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)NH₂). 5. The parent amide X containing 1 extra carbon is 2-Methylbutanamide (CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CONH₂).
Yields t-butylamine, which gives t-butanol (achiral 3° alcohol).
Benzamide contains 7 carbons and yields aniline.

solutionExplanation:
1. Amide X (C₅H₉NO) undergoes Hofmann degradation to yield 1° amine Y with one carbon less (C₄H₁₁N).
2. 1° amine Y with HNO₂ yields an optically active 2° alcohol Z (C₄H₁₀O).
3. The only optically active 2° four-carbon alcohol is Butan-2-ol (CH₃-C*H(OH)-CH₂CH₃).
4. Amine Y yielding Butan-2-ol must be sec-butylamine (CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)NH₂).
5. The parent amide X containing 1 extra carbon is 2-Methylbutanamide (CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CONH₂).
hints: Trace the optically active 4-carbon 2° alcohol back through sec-butylamine to the 5-carbon branched primary amide.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Arrange the following methyl-substituted amine species in order of INCREASING basic strength (pK_b sequence) in AQUEOUS solution:

1. NH₃ (Ammonia)
2. CH₃NH₂ (Methylamine)
3. (CH₃)₂NH (Dimethylamine)
4. (CH₃)₃N (Trimethylamine)

options.explanation: In aqueous solution, basicity of methyl-substituted amines follows the 213 Order: (CH₃)₂NH (2°) > CH₃NH₂ (1°) > (CH₃)₃N (3°) > NH₃. Therefore, in order of INCREASING basic strength (weakest to strongest): NH₃ (1) < (CH₃)₃N (4) < CH₃NH₂ (2) < (CH₃)₂NH (3), which corresponds to 1 < 4 < 2 < 3.
Decreasing order instead of increasing.
Gas-phase order, not aqueous.
Incorrect basicity sequence.

solutionExplanation:
In aqueous solution, basicity of methyl-substituted amines follows the 213 Order:
(CH₃)₂NH (2°) > CH₃NH₂ (1°) > (CH₃)₃N (3°) > NH₃.
Therefore, in order of INCREASING basic strength (weakest to strongest):
NH₃ (1) < (CH₃)₃N (4) < CH₃NH₂ (2) < (CH₃)₂NH (3) ⟹ 1 < 4 < 2 < 3.
hints: Mnemonic for aqueous methylamines is 213 (2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Why does direct nitration of Aniline with concentrated HNO₃ / H₂SO₄ mixture at 288 K yield an unusually high proportion (47% yield) of m-nitroaniline, alongside p-nitroaniline (51%) and o-nitroaniline (2%)?

options.text: Nitric acid acts as a strong reducing agent that cleaves the benzene ring.
options.explanation: Nitric acid is an oxidizing agent.

options.text: In strongly acidic medium, basic aniline is protonated to form the Anilinium ion (Ph-NH₃⁺), which is a powerful -I / -M meta-director.
options.explanation: In the strongly acidic nitrating mixture (H₂SO₄), the basic amino group of aniline accepts a proton to form the Anilinium Ion (Ph-NH₃⁺). The positive charge on nitrogen makes the anilinium ion a powerful -I / -M Meta-Director, directing incoming nitronium ions (NO₂⁺) to the meta position (47%).

options.text: The -NH₂ group undergoes 1,2-methyl shift during nitration.
options.explanation: There are no methyl groups on aniline.

options.text: m-nitroaniline is formed by a free radical pathway.
options.explanation: Nitration is electrophilic aromatic substitution (S_EAr).

solutionExplanation: In the strongly acidic nitrating mixture (H₂SO₄), the basic amino group of aniline accepts a proton to form the Anilinium Ion (Ph-NH₃⁺). The positive charge on nitrogen makes the anilinium ion a powerful -I / -M Meta-Director, directing incoming nitronium ions (NO₂⁺) to the meta position (47%).
hints: Strongly acidic conditions protonate the amine to an anilinium ion with a full positive charge on nitrogen.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What is the active electrophilic species involved in the Carbylamine Test when a primary amine (1°) is heated with Chloroform (CHCl₃) and alcoholic KOH?

options.explanation: Electrophile in aromatic nitration.

Base (OH⁻) abstracts an acidic proton from CHCl₃ to yield the trichloromethyl anion (:CCl₃⁻), which undergoes α-elimination of Cl⁻ to generate the neutral 6-electron electrophile Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂). The 1° amine lone pair attacks :CCl₂, eventually yielding the foul-smelling Isocyanide (R-NC).
Precursor intermediate before α-elimination.
Not formed in this reaction.

solutionExplanation: Base (OH⁻) abstracts an acidic proton from CHCl₃ to yield the trichloromethyl anion (:CCl₃⁻), which undergoes α-elimination of Cl⁻ to generate the neutral 6-electron electrophile Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂). The 1° amine lone pair attacks :CCl₂, eventually yielding the foul-smelling Isocyanide (R-NC).
hints: α-Elimination of HCl from chloroform generates a neutral 6-electron divalent carbon intermediate.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Benzenediazonium chloride (Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻) is coupled with Phenol (Ph-OH) in aqueous medium at pH 9–10. What is the chemical structure, color, and name of the resulting azo dye product?

options.explanation: Formed by coupling diazonium with aniline at pH 4–5.

Coupling of benzenediazonium cation with Phenol in faintly basic medium (pH 9–10, which converts phenol to the reactive phenoxide ion) occurs at the para-position to yield p-Hydroxyazobenzene, which is an Orange Azo Dye.
Incorrect coupling product.
Product of aniline oxidation.

solutionExplanation: Coupling of benzenediazonium cation with Phenol in faintly basic medium (pH 9–10, which converts phenol to the reactive phenoxide ion) occurs at the para-position to yield p-Hydroxyazobenzene, which is an Orange Azo Dye.
hints: Coupling with phenol in basic medium yields an orange p-hydroxy azo dye.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What reagent is used in the Balz-Schiemann reaction to convert Benzenediazonium chloride into Fluorobenzene (Ph-F)?

options.explanation: Copper fluoride does not participate in a Sandmeyer-type reaction for fluorine.

options.text: Fluoroboric Acid (HBF₄) followed by thermal decomposition (Δ)
options.explanation: In the Balz-Schiemann Reaction, benzenediazonium chloride is reacted with Fluoroboric Acid (HBF₄) to precipitate benzenediazonium fluoroborate (Ph-N₂⁺BF₄⁻), which is isolated, dried, and heated gently (Δ) to undergo nitrogen loss yielding Fluorobenzene (Ph-F) + N₂ ↑ + BF₃.
Aryl diazonium does not react directly with NaF.
Incorrect reagent.

solutionExplanation: In the Balz-Schiemann Reaction, benzenediazonium chloride is reacted with Fluoroboric Acid (HBF₄) to precipitate benzenediazonium fluoroborate (Ph-N₂⁺BF₄⁻), which is isolated, dried, and heated gently (Δ) to undergo nitrogen loss yielding Fluorobenzene (Ph-F) + N₂ ↑ + BF₃.
hints: HBF₄ precipitates the diazonium fluoroborate which undergoes thermal fluorination.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: An unknown amine Z (C₃H₉N) reacts with Benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg Reagent) to form a solid derivative that is completely INSOLUBLE in aqueous NaOH solution. What is the structural formula of amine Z?

options.explanation: 1° amine, forms an N-H sulfonamide that is soluble in NaOH.

1° amines react with Hinsberg reagent to form N-alkylbenzenesulfonamides containing acidic N-H, making them soluble in NaOH. 2° amines react to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamides lacking N-H, making them INSOLUBLE in NaOH. 3° amines do not react. Among C₃H₉N isomers, N-Methylethanamine (CH₃NH-CH₂CH₃) is a Secondary (2°) amine, so its Hinsberg derivative is insoluble in NaOH.
3° amine, does not react with Hinsberg reagent.
1° amine, forms an NaOH-soluble sulfonamide.

solutionExplanation:
• 1° amines react with Hinsberg reagent to form N-alkylbenzenesulfonamides containing acidic N-H, making them soluble in NaOH.
• 2° amines react to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamides lacking N-H, making them INSOLUBLE in NaOH.
• 3° amines do not react.
Among C₃H₉N isomers, N-Methylethanamine (CH₃NH-CH₂CH₃) is a Secondary (2°) amine, so its Hinsberg derivative is insoluble in NaOH.
hints: A 2° amine forms a sulfonamide lacking an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen, rendering it insoluble in base.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What organic product is formed when Benzenediazonium chloride (Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻) is treated with Hypophosphorous Acid (H₃PO₂) in the presence of Cuprous ions?

options.explanation: Formed by warming diazonium with water.

Hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂) (or ethanol) acts as a mild reducing agent that replaces the diazonium group (-N₂⁺Cl⁻) with hydrogen, converting benzenediazonium chloride into Benzene (C₆H₆): Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻ + H₃PO₂ + H₂O ──► C₆H₆ + N₂ ↑ + H₃PO₃ + HCl.
Formed by reduction with SnCl₂/HCl.
Formed in Sandmeyer reaction with Cu₂Cl₂/HCl.

solutionExplanation:
Hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂) (or ethanol) acts as a mild reducing agent that replaces the diazonium group (-N₂⁺Cl⁻) with hydrogen, converting benzenediazonium chloride into Benzene (C₆H₆):
Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻ + H₃PO₂ + H₂O ──► C₆H₆ + N₂ ↑ + H₃PO₃ + HCl.
hints: H₃PO₂ acts as a mild reducing agent replacing -N₂⁺ with -H.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Why can unsymmetrically substituted tertiary amines (N R₁ R₂ R₃) NOT be resolved into optically active enantiomers at room temperature, despite possessing a chiral sp³-hybridized nitrogen atom?

options.text: They undergo rapid S_N2 inversion with atmospheric oxygen.
options.explanation: Oxygen is not involved in conformational inversion.

options.text: They undergo rapid Pyramidal Inversion (Umbrella Inversion) at room temperature via a planar sp² transition state (E_a ≈ 25 kJ/mol), causing complete racemization.
options.explanation: The nitrogen lone pair in tertiary amines undergoes rapid Pyramidal (Umbrella) Inversion at room temperature (10¹¹ times/sec) through a low-energy planar sp² transition state (E_a ≈ 25 kJ/mol). This rapid oscillation continuously interconverts the two enantiomeric pyramid forms, causing spontaneous complete racemization.

options.text: Tertiary amines are planar molecules with a 120° bond angle.
options.explanation: Tertiary amines are pyramidal (sp³), not planar.
Nitrogen-14 is stable.

solutionExplanation: The nitrogen lone pair in tertiary amines undergoes rapid Pyramidal (Umbrella) Inversion at room temperature (10¹¹ times/sec) through a low-energy planar sp² transition state (E_a ≈ 25 kJ/mol). This rapid oscillation continuously interconverts the two enantiomeric pyramid forms, causing spontaneous complete racemization.
hints: Low activation barrier (25 kJ/mol) allows rapid umbrella inversion through a planar sp² transition state.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: How many total moles of NaOH are consumed per mole of primary amide during the Hofmann Bromamide Degradation reaction?

options.explanation: Insufficient for deprotonation, neutralization, and hydrolysis.
Consumed only in initial bromination and deprotonation.
The balanced equation for Hofmann Bromamide degradation is: R-CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4 NaOH ──► R-NH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2 NaBr + 2 H₂O. Exactly 4 moles of NaOH are consumed per mole of amide.
More than stoichiometric requirement.

solutionExplanation:
The balanced equation for Hofmann Bromamide degradation is:
R-CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4 NaOH ──► R-NH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2 NaBr + 2 H₂O.
Exactly 4 moles of NaOH are consumed per mole of amide.
hints: 4 moles of base are required to generate 1 mole of Na₂CO₃ and 2 moles of NaBr.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following primary amines CANNOT be synthesized using the Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Aromatic amine, aryl halides fail S_N2 with phthalimide anion.
Aromatic amine, 4-bromotoluene fails S_N2.
Aliphatic 1° amine, synthesized in high purity.
Aliphatic 1° amine, synthesized in high purity.

solutionExplanation:
• A and B are correct: Aromatic 1° amines (Aniline, p-toluidine) CANNOT be prepared by Gabriel synthesis because aryl halides (Ar-X) do not undergo S_N2 nucleophilic substitution with the potassium phthalimide anion.
• C and D are incorrect: Ethylamine and Methylamine are aliphatic 1° amines and are prepared in high purity by Gabriel synthesis.
keyFormulae: \text{Gabriel Limitation: Aryl Halides (Ar-X) do NOT undergo } S_N2 \text{ substitution}
hints: Aromatic amines cannot be synthesized by Gabriel synthesis because aryl halides fail S_N2.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the valid statements regarding the basicity of Anilines and substituted Anilines: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Aniline (pK_b = 9.38) is a much weaker base than Ammonia (pK_b = 4.75) due to +M resonance delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the aromatic ring.
options.explanation: Resonance delocalization into 5 canonicals decreases lone pair availability.

options.text: Electron-donating groups (+M / +I: -OCH₃, -CH₃) at the para-position INCREASE the basic strength of aniline.
options.explanation: EDG increases electron density on nitrogen.

options.text: Almost all ortho-substituted anilines are WEAKER bases than Aniline due to the Ortho-Effect.
options.explanation: Steric hindrance to protonation and loss of coplanarity weaken basicity.

options.text: Anilinium ion (Ph-NH₃⁺) is more resonance-stabilized than neutral Aniline.
options.explanation: Neutral Aniline has 5 canonicals; Anilinium ion has only 2 canonicals.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Lone pair delocalization weakens aniline basicity; +M/+I groups increase basicity; o-substituted anilines show the Ortho-Effect (weaker base).
• D is incorrect: Neutral Aniline is stabilized by 5 canonical structures, whereas the Anilinium ion is stabilized by only 2 canonical structures (delocalization is blocked because nitrogen has no free lone pair).
hints: Delocalization across 5 canonicals stabilizes neutral aniline more than the anilinium ion.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following chemical reactions convert a primary Amide (R-CONH₂) or Nitrile (R-CN) into a Primary Amine (1°) WITHOUT changing the total number of carbon atoms? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Reduction of R-CONH₂ using LiAlH₄ in dry ether
options.explanation: RCONH₂ ──► RCH₂NH₂ (same carbon count).

options.text: Reduction of R-CN using LiAlH₄ or Na / EtOH (Mendius Reduction)
options.explanation: RCN ──► RCH₂NH₂ (same carbon count).

options.text: Hofmann Bromamide Degradation of R-CONH₂ using Br₂ / NaOH
options.explanation: Hofmann degradation LOSES 1 carbon atom.

options.text: Hydrolysis of R-CN with dilute HCl
options.explanation: Yields a Carboxylic Acid (RCOOH), not an amine.

solutionExplanation:
• A and B are correct: Reduction of amides (RCONH₂ ──► RCH₂NH₂) and nitriles (RCN ──► RCH₂NH₂) retains the exact original carbon count.
• C is incorrect: Hofmann bromamide degradation LOSES 1 carbon atom (RCONH₂ ──► RNH₂).
• D is incorrect: Hydrolysis of nitriles yields a Carboxylic Acid (RCOOH), NOT an amine.
hints: LiAlH₄ reduction preserves the carbon count; Hofmann degradation eliminates one carbon.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct statements regarding the Sandmeyer and Gattermann reactions of Arenediazonium Salts: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Sandmeyer reaction utilizes Cuprous salts (Cu₂Cl₂ / HCl or Cu₂Br₂ / HBr) to replace -N₂⁺ with halogens.
options.explanation: Cu(I) salts catalyze displacement.

options.text: Gattermann reaction utilizes fine Copper powder in the presence of HX (Cu / HCl or Cu / HBr).
options.explanation: Uses metallic copper powder.

options.text: Sandmeyer reactions generally yield higher percentage product recoveries than Gattermann reactions.
options.explanation: Cuprous salts give superior yields.

options.text: Both reactions proceed via an S_N2 backside inversion mechanism on the benzene ring.
options.explanation: Both reactions proceed via Aryl Free Radical intermediates (Ar•), not S_N2.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Sandmeyer uses Cu₂X₂ (higher yield); Gattermann uses Cu powder/HX.
• D is incorrect: Both reactions proceed via Aryl Free Radical intermediates (Ar•), NOT S_N2 backside inversion.
hints: Both reactions proceed through aryl free radicals, with Sandmeyer giving higher yields.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following tests can be used to distinguish Primary (1°) Aliphatic Amines from Secondary (2°) Aliphatic Amines? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: 1° amines give foul R-NC; 2° amines do not react.

options.text: Reaction with Nitrous Acid (HNO₂ at 0–5°C) releasing N₂ gas
options.explanation: 1° amines liberate N₂ gas; 2° amines form yellow oily nitrosamines.

options.text: Solubility of Benzenesulfonamide derivative in aqueous NaOH (Hinsberg Test)
options.explanation: 1° derivative is soluble in NaOH; 2° derivative is insoluble.
Biuret test is for peptide bonds in proteins, not simple amines.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: 1° amines give foul-smelling isocyanides in carbylamine test, release N₂ gas with HNO₂, and form NaOH-soluble Hinsberg derivatives. 2° amines fail carbylamine, form yellow nitrosamines with HNO₂, and form NaOH-insoluble Hinsberg derivatives.
• D is incorrect: Biuret test is used to detect peptide bonds in proteins, NOT simple amines.
hints: Biuret is for protein peptide linkages; Carbylamine, HNO₂, and Hinsberg distinguish 1° from 2° amines.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct options regarding the Azo Coupling reactions of Benzenediazonium Chloride (Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻): (Select all that apply)

options.text: Coupling with Phenol is performed in weakly basic medium (pH 9–10) to form p-Hydroxyazobenzene (Orange Dye).
options.explanation: Basic pH generates reactive phenoxide.

options.text: Coupling with Aniline is performed in weakly acidic medium (pH 4–5) to form p-Aminoazobenzene (Yellow Dye).
options.explanation: Acidic pH optimizes free aniline nucleophile vs diazonium stability.

options.text: The diazonium cation (Ph-N₂⁺) acts as a weak electrophile attacking the para-position of activated aromatic rings.
options.explanation: Weak electrophile in S_EAr.

options.text: Azo coupling destroys the aromaticity of both benzene rings permanently.
options.explanation: Azo coupling PRESERVES the aromaticity of both rings, forming an extended conjugated system.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Phenol couples at pH 9–10 (orange dye); Aniline couples at pH 4–5 (yellow dye); Ph-N₂⁺ acts as an electrophile in S_EAr.
• D is incorrect: Azo coupling PRESERVES the aromaticity of both benzene rings, generating extended conjugated π-systems that absorb visible light.
hints: Coupling with phenol requires basic pH 9–10; coupling with aniline requires acidic pH 4–5.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following reagents can reduce Nitrobenzene (C₆H₅NO₂) into Aniline (C₆H₅NH₂)? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Preferred industrial reduction (FeCl₂ hydrolyzes to regenerate HCl).
Classic laboratory reducing agent.

options.text: H₂ gas in the presence of Raney Nickel or Palladium catalyst
options.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation.
Reduces to azoxybenzene/azobenzene, not aniline.

solutionExplanation: • A, B, C are correct: Fe/HCl, Sn/HCl, and catalytic hydrogenation (H₂/Ni or Pd) efficiently reduce nitro groups to primary aromatic amines. (Fe/HCl is preferred industrially because FeCl₂ formed hydrolyzes to release HCl, minimizing required acid).
hints: Fe/HCl, Sn/HCl, and catalytic H₂/Pd convert -NO₂ directly to -NH₂.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct options regarding Quaternary Ammonium Salts (N⁺ R₁ R₂ R₃ R₄ X⁻): (Select all that apply)

options.text: The central nitrogen atom is sp³-hybridized and lacks a non-bonding lone pair.
options.explanation: All 4 orbitals are engaged in σ-bonds.

options.text: Unsymmetrically substituted quaternary ammonium cations (N⁺ R₁ R₂ R₃ R₄) are CHIRAL and can be resolved into optically active enantiomers.
options.explanation: Rigid tetrahedral geometry with 4 different groups confers chirality.

options.text: They do not undergo pyramidal inversion at room temperature.
options.explanation: Lacking a lone pair, umbrella inversion cannot occur.

options.text: They react rapidly with Hinsberg reagent to form soluble nitrosamines.
options.explanation: Quaternary ammonium salts do not react with Hinsberg reagent (Ph-SO₂Cl).

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: 4° ammonium salts have no lone pair, cannot undergo pyramidal inversion, and are chiral when 4 different R-groups are attached.
• D is incorrect: Quaternary ammonium salts do NOT react with Hinsberg reagent (Ph-SO₂Cl).
hints: Absence of a lone pair locks the sp³ tetrahedral geometry and prevents pyramidal inversion.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following functional groups exert a META-DIRECTING DEACTIVATING influence during electrophilic aromatic substitution of anilines or substituted benzenes? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Positive charge on nitrogen exerts strong -I effect, directing meta.
Strong -M and -I meta-director.
Strong -M and -I meta-director.
-OH is a powerful +M Ortho/Para-directing Activator.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: -NH₃⁺, -NO₂, and -CN are powerful -I/-M groups that deactivate the ring and direct electrophiles to the meta position.
• D is incorrect: -OH is a powerful +M Ortho/Para-directing Activator.
hints: -NH₃⁺, -NO₂, and -CN withdraw electron density and direct meta.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct statements regarding the physical and chemical properties of Sulfanilic Acid: (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is prepared by heating Aniline with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 453–473 K.
options.explanation: Established synthesis of sulfanilic acid.

options.text: It exists as a dipolar internal Zwitterion (⁺H₃N-C₆H₄-SO₃⁻).
options.explanation: Proton transfers from sulfonic acid to amino group.

options.text: The Zwitterionic form contains an acidic -SO₃⁻ group and a basic -NH₃⁺ group.
options.explanation: -NH₃⁺ is the acidic proton donor; -SO₃⁻ is the basic conjugate base.

options.text: It is insoluble in organic solvents but soluble in aqueous strong bases (NaOH).
options.explanation: Reacts with NaOH to form soluble sodium sulfanilate salt.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, D are correct: Sulfanilic acid is prepared at 453–473 K, forms a Zwitterion, is insoluble in organic solvents, and dissolves in NaOH (forming sodium sulfanilate salt).
• C is incorrect: In the Zwitterion ⁺H₃N-C₆H₄-SO₃⁻, the -NH₃⁺ group is ACIDIC (proton donor) and the -SO₃⁻ group is BASIC (proton acceptor).
hints: In the zwitterion, -NH₃⁺ is the acid and -SO₃⁻ is the conjugate base.
